exercises.name: Incline Barbell Press
instructions: Lie back on a bench set to roughly 30 to 45 degrees and take a grip a little wider than your shoulders.
Unrack the bar and hold it over your upper chest with your shoulder blades pulled back and down.
Lower the bar under control to your upper chest with your forearms vertical.
Press back up until your arms are straight without letting your shoulders roll forward.
exercises.formCue: Shoulder blades pinned, bar to the collarbone line.
exercises.commonMistakes: Setting the bench too steep so it becomes a shoulder press, and bouncing the bar off the chest.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the incline machine press or light dumbbells until the bar path feels steady.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It loads the upper chest harder than a flat press does.

exercises.name: Decline Barbell Press
exercises.musclesWorked: Lower and mid chest, triceps, front delts
instructions: Hook your feet under the leg brace and lie back on the decline bench.
Grip the bar a little wider than your shoulders and unrack it over your chest.
Lower the bar under control to your lower chest.
Press back up until your arms are straight, then re-rack with a spotter's help if the load is heavy.
exercises.formCue: Feet locked in, bar to the lower chest.
exercises.commonMistakes: Lowering the bar toward the neck and unracking heavy loads without a spotter.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with the decline machine press or a light bar and a spotter.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It lets you press heavy through the lower chest with less shoulder strain for many lifters.

exercises.name: Incline Machine Press
instructions: Set the seat so the handles sit just below your upper chest.
Grip the handles with your elbows out to the sides and your back flat on the pad.
Press the handles up and away until your arms are straight.
Return slowly until you feel a light stretch across the chest, then repeat.
exercises.formCue: Chest up, press on the machine's line.
exercises.commonMistakes: Seat set too low so the shoulders take over, and letting the stack slam between reps.
exercises.beginnerModification: Drop the weight and pause for a second at the stretch on every rep.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A fixed path lets you push the upper chest hard without balancing a bar.

exercises.name: Decline Machine Press
exercises.musclesWorked: Lower and mid chest, triceps, front delts
instructions: Set the seat so the handles line up with your lower chest.
Sit tall with your back on the pad and grip the handles.
Press the handles forward and down until your arms are straight.
Return slowly until your chest is lightly stretched, then repeat.
exercises.formCue: Shoulders down, drive through the palms.
exercises.commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulders forward at lockout and cutting the range short.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter load and a three-second lowering phase.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the lower chest hard with a stable, easy setup.

exercises.name: Pec Deck Fly
instructions: Set the seat so your upper arms are level with your shoulders when you hold the pads or handles.
Sit with your back on the pad and your elbows slightly bent.
Bring your arms together in front of your chest in a wide hugging arc.
Open back slowly until you feel a comfortable stretch across the chest, then repeat.
exercises.formCue: Hug a barrel, squeeze the chest.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the arms swing too far back and turning the fly into a press by bending the elbows.
exercises.beginnerModification: Shorten the range and use a load you can pause at the squeeze.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It isolates the chest without the triceps giving out first.

exercises.name: Low-to-High Cable Fly
instructions: Set both pulleys low and stand between them with a handle in each hand.
Take a small step forward and keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Sweep your hands up and in until they meet in front of your upper chest.
Lower along the same arc under control and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Scoop up and in, elbows soft.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending the elbows to curl the weight and shrugging the shoulders at the top.
exercises.beginnerModification: Work one arm at a time with a light load.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The upward arc keeps tension on the upper chest through the whole rep.

exercises.name: High-to-Low Cable Fly
exercises.musclesWorked: Lower and mid chest, front delts
instructions: Set both pulleys high and stand between them with a handle in each hand.
Step forward into a split stance and lean your torso slightly forward.
With a slight elbow bend, bring your hands down and together in front of your hips.
Let your arms travel back up slowly until your chest is stretched, then repeat.
exercises.formCue: Hands meet at the hips, chest tall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pressing the handles down with bent elbows and rounding the shoulders forward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Reduce the load and pause where the hands meet.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The downward arc lines up with the lower chest fibres.

exercises.name: T-Bar Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, mid back, rear delts, biceps
exercises.equipment: T-bar row station or landmine with handle
instructions: Stand over the bar with your knees slightly bent and hinge forward with a flat back.
Grip the handles and lift the weight clear of the floor.
Pull the handles to your torso, driving your elbows back.
Lower until your arms are straight and your shoulders stretch forward, keeping your back flat.
exercises.formCue: Flat back, elbows to the hips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing up with each rep and rounding the lower back as the set gets hard.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the chest-supported version so your lower back is not the limit.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It lets you row heavy on a fixed arc and build back thickness.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, mid back, rear delts, biceps
instructions: Sit at the cable row with your knees slightly bent and hold the handle in one hand.
Let the shoulder reach forward while your torso stays tall.
Pull the handle to the side of your waist and draw the shoulder blade back.
Return until the arm is straight, finish the reps, then switch sides.
exercises.formCue: Elbow to the back pocket.
exercises.commonMistakes: Twisting the whole torso to move the weight and shrugging the shoulder up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lower the load and hold the squeeze for one second on every rep.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Training one side at a time gives a longer range and shows up side-to-side gaps.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, teres major, rear delts, biceps
instructions: Grip the bar well outside shoulder width with palms facing away and lock your thighs under the pad.
Start with arms straight and your chest lifted.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, driving your elbows down and out.
Let the bar rise until your arms are straight and your lats are stretched.
exercises.formCue: Chest to the bar, elbows down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning far back to swing the weight and pulling the bar behind the neck.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter load and a slightly narrower grip.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The wide grip builds the outer lats that give the back its width.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.equipment: Lat pulldown machine, close parallel handle
instructions: Attach a close parallel-grip handle and lock your thighs under the pad.
Start with your arms straight overhead and your chest lifted.
Pull the handle to your upper chest, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Return slowly until your arms are straight and your lats are stretched.
exercises.formCue: Elbows brush the ribs.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rocking back for momentum and stopping short of a full stretch at the top.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lower the weight and count two seconds on the way up.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The close grip gives a long range of motion for the lats.

exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.equipment: Lat pulldown machine, wide parallel-grip bar
instructions: Attach a bar with parallel handles and grip it with your palms facing each other.
Lock your thighs under the pad and start with your arms straight.
Pull the bar to your upper chest with your elbows tracking down in front of your sides.
Return under control to a full stretch.
exercises.formCue: Palms in, chest up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Shrugging at the top and using body swing to finish the rep.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a load you can pause at the chest for one second.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A palms-in grip is often the most comfortable way to load the lats.

exercises.name: Seated Machine Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Mid back, lats, rear delts, biceps
instructions: Set the seat so the handles are level with your lower chest and the chest pad lets you just reach them.
Sit tall with your chest on the pad and grip the handles.
Pull back until your elbows pass your torso and your shoulder blades squeeze together.
Return until your arms are straight and your shoulders reach forward.
exercises.formCue: Chest on the pad, squeeze the blades.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pulling the chest off the pad and cutting the stretch short.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lower the weight and pause at the squeeze.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The chest pad removes the lower back from the lift so the upper back does the work.

exercises.name: Machine Pullover
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, teres major, rear delts, long head of triceps
instructions: Set the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine's pivot and fasten the belt if there is one.
Place your elbows on the pads and hold the bar lightly.
Drive your elbows forward and down until they reach your sides.
Let the arms travel back overhead slowly to a comfortable stretch.
exercises.formCue: Push with the elbows, not the hands.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pulling with the hands and arching the lower back at the stretch.
exercises.beginnerModification: Shorten the overhead range and use a light load.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It works the lats through a long range without the biceps limiting the set.

exercises.name: Rack Pull
exercises.musclesWorked: Spinal erectors, traps, glutes, hamstrings, grip
instructions: Set the rack pins so the bar rests around knee height.
Stand with the bar against your legs, hinge to grip it and set a flat back.
Stand up by driving your hips forward until you are fully upright.
Lower the bar to the pins under control and reset before the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Flat back, hips through.
exercises.commonMistakes: Loading far more than you can hold with a flat back and dropping the bar onto the pins.
exercises.beginnerModification: Raise the pins slightly and use a load you could also lift from the floor.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The short range lets you load the upper back and traps heavily.

exercises.name: Reverse-Grip Barbell Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, mid back, rear delts, biceps
instructions: Hold the bar with a shoulder-width underhand grip.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward with a flat back.
Pull the bar to your waist with your elbows close to your sides.
Lower until your arms are straight without letting your back round.
exercises.formCue: Palms up, bar to the belt.
exercises.commonMistakes: Jerking the torso upright and curling the bar with the wrists.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the chest-supported row or a lighter bar.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The underhand grip keeps the elbows tight and brings in more lats and biceps.

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.musclesWorked: Front and side delts, triceps, upper traps
instructions: Set the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height.
Sit with your back on the pad and grip the handles.
Press up until your arms are straight overhead.
Lower slowly until your hands are back at shoulder level.
exercises.formCue: Ribs down, press to the ceiling.
exercises.commonMistakes: Arching the lower back off the pad and stopping the lowering phase early.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light load and a seat height that feels easy on the shoulders.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A guided path lets you train the delts close to failure safely.

exercises.name: Machine Lateral Raise
instructions: Set the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine's pivots.
Sit with your arms bent and the pads against the outside of your arms.
Raise your arms out to the sides until your upper arms are level with the floor.
Lower slowly and stop just before the weight rests.
exercises.formCue: Lead with the elbows.
exercises.commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up and bouncing out of the bottom.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter load and a two-second pause at the top.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The machine keeps even tension on the side delts through the whole range.

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck
exercises.equipment: Pec deck machine set for reverse fly
instructions: Sit facing the pad and set the seat so your arms are level with your shoulders.
Hold the handles with your chest against the pad and your elbows slightly bent.
Sweep your arms out and back until they are in line with your shoulders.
Return slowly without letting the weight rest.
exercises.formCue: Wide arms, elbows high.
exercises.commonMistakes: Using too much weight and turning it into a row by bending the elbows.
exercises.beginnerModification: Go lighter and stop the arc at shoulder line.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It isolates the rear delts, which pressing and rowing often leave behind.

exercises.name: Upright Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Side delts, front delts, traps, biceps
instructions: Stand tall holding the bar with an overhand grip a little wider than your shoulders.
Pull the bar up along your body with your elbows leading.
Stop when your elbows reach about shoulder height.
Lower under control until your arms are straight.
exercises.formCue: Elbows lead, stop at the shoulders.
exercises.commonMistakes: Using a narrow grip and pulling the elbows well above shoulder height.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a cable or dumbbells with a wider hand position and a shorter range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the side delts and traps together with one heavy pull.

exercises.name: Cable Y Raise
exercises.musclesWorked: Side delts, front delts, lower traps
instructions: Set both pulleys low and take the left handle in your right hand and the right handle in your left.
Step back slightly and stand tall with your elbows a little bent.
Raise your arms up and out into a Y until your elbows are level with your ears.
Lower slowly along the same path.
exercises.formCue: Reach long, thumbs up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning back to heave the load and shrugging toward the ears.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it one arm at a time with the lightest plate.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The cable keeps tension on the delts at the bottom, where dumbbells go slack.

exercises.name: Cable Reverse Fly
instructions: Set both pulleys at about shoulder height and take the left cable in your right hand and the right in your left.
Step back so your arms are crossed in front of you with elbows slightly bent.
Pull your arms out and back until they are in line with your shoulders.
Return slowly until your hands cross again.
exercises.formCue: Pull apart, keep the elbows up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending the elbows to row the weight and arching the lower back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the reverse pec deck so the machine guides the arc.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It loads the rear delts with steady tension and no bench needed.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Sit back on a bench set to about 45 to 60 degrees with a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang straight down behind your torso.
Curl the weights, turning your palms up, until your forearms are vertical.
Lower slowly to a full hang and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Elbows stay back, full hang.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the elbows drift forward and lifting the shoulders off the bench.
exercises.beginnerModification: Raise the bench angle and use lighter dumbbells.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The arm-behind-body position trains the biceps in a stretched position.

exercises.name: Spider Curl
exercises.equipment: EZ bar or barbell, incline bench
instructions: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with your shoulders near the top.
Hold the bar with a shoulder-width underhand grip and let your arms hang straight down.
Curl the bar up without moving your upper arms.
Lower until your arms are straight and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Upper arms hang still.
exercises.commonMistakes: Swinging the upper arms back and stopping short of full extension.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use dumbbells or a lighter bar and slow the lowering phase.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The bench takes away body swing so the elbow flexors do all the work.

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Curl
instructions: Stand tall holding the bar on the angled grips with your palms up.
Keep your elbows at your sides and curl the bar until your forearms are vertical.
Squeeze briefly at the top.
Lower until your arms are straight.
exercises.formCue: Elbows pinned, no lean.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning back to swing the bar and letting the elbows drift forward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Stand with your back against a wall and use a lighter bar.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The angled grip lets you load the biceps with less wrist strain than a straight bar.

exercises.name: Reverse Curl
instructions: Stand tall holding the bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Keep your elbows at your sides and curl the bar until your forearms are vertical.
Keep your wrists straight through the lift.
Lower until your arms are straight.
exercises.formCue: Knuckles up, wrists straight.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the wrists bend back and using a load meant for regular curls.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use an EZ bar and about half your normal curl weight.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The palms-down grip builds the top of the forearm and the brachialis.

exercises.name: Cable Rope Hammer Curl
instructions: Attach a rope to a low pulley and hold an end in each hand with your palms facing each other.
Stand tall with your arms straight and your elbows at your sides.
Curl the rope up until your forearms are vertical.
Lower until your arms are straight.
exercises.formCue: Thumbs up, elbows still.
exercises.commonMistakes: Stepping too close so the cable goes slack and rocking the torso.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lower the load and pause at the top.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The cable keeps tension on the arm at the bottom of the curl.

exercises.name: Machine Triceps Dip
instructions: Sit with your back against the pad and fasten the belt if there is one.
Grip the handles with your elbows pointing straight back.
Push the handles down until your arms are straight.
Let the handles rise slowly until your shoulders feel a light stretch.
exercises.formCue: Elbows back, lock it out.
exercises.commonMistakes: Flaring the elbows wide and letting the shoulders shrug up at the top.
exercises.beginnerModification: Shorten the top range and use a lighter stack.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It gives the heavy loading of a dip without having to carry your bodyweight.

exercises.name: Tricep Kickback
instructions: Place one knee and the same-side hand on a bench with your back flat.
Hold a dumbbell in the other hand and lift your upper arm until it is level with the floor.
Straighten your elbow until the whole arm is in line.
Bend the elbow back to the start without dropping the upper arm.
exercises.formCue: Upper arm stays level.
exercises.commonMistakes: Swinging the upper arm and using a weight too heavy to lock out.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a very light dumbbell and pause at full extension.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It works the triceps hardest at full lockout with very little load on the joints.

exercises.name: JM Press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench and unrack the bar with a shoulder-width or slightly narrower grip.
Lower the bar in a straight line toward your upper chest and neck area while your elbows bend and stay fairly high.
Stop when your forearms meet your biceps.
Press the bar back up until your arms are straight.
exercises.formCue: Elbows up, fold and press.
exercises.commonMistakes: Starting too heavy and letting the elbows drop so it turns into a close-grip bench press.
exercises.beginnerModification: Learn the path with an empty bar or use the close-grip bench press.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It blends a press and an extension so the triceps can be loaded heavily.

exercises.name: Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit and rest your forearms on your thighs with your palms up and your wrists just past your knees.
Hold the bar with a narrow underhand grip and let it roll down toward your fingers.
Close your grip and curl your knuckles up as high as you can.
Lower slowly and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Forearms down, move only the wrists.
exercises.commonMistakes: Lifting the forearms off the thighs and rushing the reps.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light dumbbell one hand at a time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the inner forearm and grip.

exercises.name: Reverse Wrist Curl
instructions: Sit and rest your forearms on your thighs with your palms down and your wrists just past your knees.
Hold the bar with an overhand grip.
Raise your knuckles as high as you can.
Lower until your knuckles point toward the floor and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Knuckles to the ceiling.
exercises.commonMistakes: Going too heavy and letting the forearms lift off the thighs.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a very light dumbbell one hand at a time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the back of the forearm, which most pulling work misses.

exercises.name: Hack Squat
instructions: Lie back on the pad with your shoulders under the shoulder pads and your feet about shoulder-width on the platform.
Straighten your legs and release the safety handles.
Lower by bending your knees and hips as deep as you can control with your back on the pad.
Push through your whole foot until your legs are straight, then re-engage the safeties when done.
exercises.formCue: Back on the pad, knees over toes.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the knees cave in and the hips lift off the pad at the bottom.
exercises.beginnerModification: Shorten the depth and use only the sled weight to start.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The back support lets you load the quads hard without balance being the limit.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Squat
instructions: Set the bar at upper-chest height and place it across the back of your shoulders.
Stand with your feet under or slightly in front of the bar and rotate it off the hooks.
Squat by bending your hips and knees until your thighs are about level with the floor.
Stand up until your legs are straight and rotate the bar back onto the hooks when done.
exercises.formCue: Knees follow the toes.
exercises.commonMistakes: Placing the feet so far forward that the lower back rounds, and letting the knees cave in.
exercises.beginnerModification: Squat to a bench set at a comfortable depth.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The guided bar lets you take the quads close to failure without a spotter.

exercises.name: High-Foot Leg Press
instructions: Sit in the leg press and place your feet shoulder-width on the upper part of the platform.
Straighten your legs and release the safeties.
Lower the platform until your hips are deeply bent while your lower back stays on the pad.
Push through your heels until your legs are nearly straight.
exercises.formCue: Hips stay down, drive the heels.
exercises.commonMistakes: Going so deep that the hips roll off the pad and locking the knees hard at the top.
exercises.beginnerModification: Reduce the depth and the load until your lower back stays flat.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Research suggests foot position changes muscle activity only modestly, with a higher placement shifting some work toward the glutes under heavy loads.

source.name: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health (systematic review of leg press EMG)

exercises.name: Single-Leg Leg Press
instructions: Sit in the leg press and place one foot in the middle of the platform with the other foot on the floor or held clear.
Straighten the working leg and release the safeties.
Lower until your knee is deeply bent while your hips stay square on the seat.
Push back up until the leg is nearly straight, finish the reps, then switch legs.
exercises.formCue: Hips square, knee tracks the toes.
exercises.commonMistakes: Twisting the hips toward the working leg and loading it like a two-leg press.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with less than half of your two-leg weight and a shorter range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It evens out strength between legs with your back fully supported.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
instructions: Sit with your back on the pad and your knees lined up with the machine's pivot.
Rest your lower legs on the roller and lock the thigh pad down.
Pull the roller down and back by bending your knees as far as you can.
Return slowly until your legs are straight.
exercises.formCue: Hips back, curl the heels under.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the hips slide forward and letting the weight snap back up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light load and a three-second return.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Curling with the hips bent trains the hamstrings at a long length.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
instructions: Lie face down with your knees just off the edge of the bench and the roller above your heels.
Hold the handles and keep your hips pressed into the pad.
Curl the roller toward the back of your thighs.
Lower slowly until your legs are straight.
exercises.formCue: Hips down, heels to glutes.
exercises.commonMistakes: Lifting the hips off the pad and using momentum out of the bottom.
exercises.beginnerModification: Reduce the load and work one leg at a time.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It isolates knee flexion, which hinges like the Romanian deadlift do not train.

exercises.name: Hip Abduction Machine
exercises.musclesWorked: Glute medius, glute minimus, upper glutes
instructions: Sit with your back on the pad and the outside of your thighs against the pads.
Hold the handles and sit tall.
Push your legs apart as far as you comfortably can.
Bring them back together slowly without letting the stack rest.
exercises.formCue: Push the knees out, pause.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bouncing through short reps and rocking the torso for momentum.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light load and hold the open position for two seconds.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the side glutes that keep the hips and knees steady.

exercises.name: Hip Adduction Machine
instructions: Sit with your back on the pad and the inside of your thighs against the pads.
Set the start position to a stretch you find comfortable.
Squeeze your legs together until the pads meet.
Open slowly back to the start.
exercises.formCue: Squeeze in, open slow.
exercises.commonMistakes: Setting the start position too wide and letting the pads fly apart.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a narrower start position and a light load.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the inner thigh directly, which squats only train in part.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
instructions: Sit with the balls of your feet on the platform and your heels hanging off.
Set the pad on your lower thighs and release the safety.
Lower your heels until your calves are stretched.
Raise your heels as high as you can, pause, and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Full stretch, full squeeze.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bouncing at the bottom and doing short half reps.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light load and pause for two seconds at the bottom.
exercises.whyThisMatters: With the knees bent the deeper calf muscle, the soleus, does most of the work.

exercises.name: Donkey Calf Raise
instructions: Stand with the balls of your feet on the block and your heels hanging off.
Hinge forward, rest your forearms on the support and set the pad on your lower back and hips.
Straighten your knees and lower your heels until your calves are stretched.
Raise your heels as high as you can, then lower slowly.
exercises.formCue: Legs straight, heels all the way down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending the knees to help and bouncing out of the stretch.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do the same hinged position with bodyweight only.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The bent-over position puts the calves under a deep stretch.

exercises.name: Leg Press Calf Raise
instructions: Sit in the leg press and straighten your legs with the safeties still engaged where the machine allows.
Slide your feet down so only the balls of your feet are on the lower edge of the platform.
Let your heels sink toward you until your calves are stretched.
Push the platform away by pointing your toes, then lower slowly.
exercises.formCue: Push through the big toe.
exercises.commonMistakes: Unlocking the safeties with the feet barely on the platform and bending the knees to help.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the safeties engaged and use a light load.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It loads the calves heavily with no weight on the spine.

exercises.name: Cable Glute Kickback
instructions: Fasten an ankle cuff to a low pulley and attach it to one ankle.
Face the machine, hold the frame and lean forward slightly with the working knee bent.
Drive the leg back by straightening your hip and knee.
Return slowly, finish the reps, then switch legs.
exercises.formCue: Squeeze the glute, keep the back still.
exercises.commonMistakes: Arching the lower back to get the leg higher and swinging the leg.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it with no cable from a hands-and-knees position.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains one glute at a time with steady cable tension.

exercises.name: 45-Degree Hip Extension
instructions: Set the pad just below your hip crease so you can bend freely at the hips, and hook your heels under the brace.
Cross your arms over your chest or hold a plate there.
Lower by bending only at the hips until you feel a mild stretch in your hamstrings.
Squeeze your glutes to raise your torso until it is in line with your legs, and stop there.
exercises.formCue: Hinge at the hips, finish with the glutes.
exercises.commonMistakes: Arching past a straight line at the top and bouncing out of the bottom.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use bodyweight and a shorter range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Moving from the hips instead of the spine puts the work on the glutes and hamstrings.

exercises.name: Cable Crunch
instructions: Kneel below a high pulley and hold the rope ends beside your head.
Keep your hips still and above your knees.
Curl your ribs toward your hips so your elbows travel toward your thighs.
Return slowly until your torso is tall again.
exercises.formCue: Curl the spine, hips stay put.
exercises.commonMistakes: Sitting the hips back and pulling with the arms.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light load and learn the curl on the floor first.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It lets you add load to the abs the way you would to any other muscle.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
instructions: Kneel on a mat and hold the wheel under your shoulders with your arms straight.
Tuck your ribs down and brace your midsection.
Roll the wheel forward as far as you can without your lower back sagging.
Pull the wheel back toward your knees to return.
exercises.formCue: Ribs down, do not let the back sag.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the lower back arch and rolling out further than you can control.
exercises.beginnerModification: Roll toward a wall that stops the wheel at a short distance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the abs to resist the lower back arching under load.

exercises.name: Decline Sit-Up
instructions: Hook your feet under the pads of a decline bench and sit with your hips bent.
Cross your arms over your chest or hold a plate there.
Lower your torso under control until your shoulders reach the bench.
Curl back up by bending at the waist and hips.
exercises.formCue: Control the way down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Throwing the arms or head forward for momentum and dropping fast.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lower the bench angle or lower only halfway.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The slope adds range and resistance to a plain sit-up.
